To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there is no contribution to the absorptive amplitude of the axial-vector vector amplitude due to the external field to the linear order.

the neutrino-photo processes, forbidden in a vacuum, become allowed in a magnetized plasma, and that the magnetic field strength affects the neutrino propagation in a medium only through the charged leptons.

the neutrino-pho-ton interactions in a magnetized medium are suppressed, compared to the vacuum, by a factor of the order of the inverse lepton mass, and that the neutrino self-energy in a magnetized plasma has a contribution of the same order of magnitude, due to the photon polarization tensor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of neutrino propagation in the presence of matter and/or a weak magnetic field.

a systematic analysis of the one-loop corrections, due to the presence in the medium of the charged leptons (both real and virtual), to the imaginary part of the neutrino-photo production and annihilation amplitudes, in a weakly-magnetized plasma.
the effects of a weak magnetic field on the absorptive part (the imaginary part) of the neutrino-photo processes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetic field does not affect the neutrino propagation in the weakly magnetized regime, at the one loop level.
, to linear order in the magnetic field, there is no modification of the axial-vector amplitudes in a magnetized plasma with respect to the vacuum.

the presence of a weakly magnetizing field does not alter the neutrino propagation, in the sense that there are no corrections to the absorptive parts of the amplitudes, to the linear orders in the magnetic field.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is no effect on the neutrino-photonic processes, at one loop level, due to the presence or absence of an external magnetic field.
the axial-vector-vector part of the neutrino self-energy is not modified in the presence of an external electro-magnet field.
the neutrino-photonic processes, forbidden in the vacuum, do not take place in a weakly magnetic medium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neutrino-photonic interactions in a magnetized plasma can be treated as perturbations to the vacuum processes.
the neutrino-photonic interaction in a weakly magnetic medium is the same as in vacuum.

the presence of an external magnetic field does not modify the neutrino-pharmon absorptive processes at the one-loop order, but it can induce the appearance of a finite absorptive part for the vector-vector amplitude.
